# ===========================================================================
# THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE TAG SET -- TWO TIERS, AND THE DIFFERENCE
# BETWEEN THEM IS A HARD API LIMIT, NOT AN EDITORIAL CHOICE.
# ===========================================================================
#
# TIER 1 -- the topics section below. GitHub repo topics, capped at TWENTY by
#   the server; the API rejects the 21st. Nothing written here changes that.
#   Each becomes a crawlable github.com/topics/<t> page, which is the highest
#   value discovery surface a repository has. Someone typing
#   "dnscrypt for android" into a search engine should land on one of these.
#
# TIER 2 -- the signature section below. The block written into EVERY
#   document. NO LIMIT. Visible markdown text is what survives GitHub's
#   sanitizer intact -- a <meta> tag is deleted outright, and display:none
#   renders visible anyway -- which makes plain "#tag" text the true
#   descendant of the old forum signature, and the right home for an
#   unlimited tag set.
#
# FORMAT, and it is load-bearing: entries are PLAIN. No leading "#", no
# trailing parenthetical. The parser treats any line beginning with "#" as a
# comment, so a tag written as "#dns" is silently DROPPED. That is measured,
# not assumed: the first version of this file wrote tags with a leading "#",
# and a local run of the validator turned every COMMENT into a candidate tag
# while losing all the real ones. Caught before it ever reached CI.
#
# THE RULE THAT GOVERNS BOTH TIERS: every tag must name something GENUINELY
# PRESENT IN THIS TREE. A tag is a claim about the repository, and a claim
# nobody checked is exactly the decoration this project refuses everywhere
# else. The Meta Hashtag Manager (.github/workflows/tag-manager.yml) verifies
# each one against the tree on every run, and suggests tags for new code.

[SIGNATURE]
# Must be a SUPERSET of the topics tier, or a topic someone searches for is
# missing from the indexed body text. Re-measure evidence with:
#   git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lIi "<tag>" | wc -l
# Measured 2026-08-01: uniffi 1199 files, dnscrypt 662, slint 135, warden 121,
# doh 101, cdn 100, blocklist 94, odoh 54, rebind 52, dnssec 49, dns64 26,
# homograph 18, svcb 17.

# ===========================================================================
# PER-DOCUMENT EXTRAS. One optional section per document basename. The Meta
# Hashtag Manager writes the signature tier into every document AND prepends
# that document's own extras, so a crawler landing on SECURITY.md from a
# search sees the security vocabulary first and the project vocabulary after
# it. An identical block on every page would teach a crawler nothing about
# which page it is on.
# ===========================================================================
